content.text: {"predictors": [{"name": "Inventory Growth Divergence", "construction": "Compute year-over-year growth in inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus year-over-year growth in cost of goods sold (COGS). Rank firms cross-sectionally each June using the most recent fiscal year data.", "rationale": "When inventories accumulate faster than sales-driven costs, it signals weakening demand and future markdowns that the market is slow to price, depressing subsequent returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (inventory growing slower than COGS)"}, {"name": "Accruals-to-Cashflow Quality", "construction": "For each firm compute (Net Income minus Cash Flow from Operations) scaled by absolute Cash Flow from Operations, using Compustat funds-flow items. Where a cash flow statement is unavailable, derive operating cash flow from changes in working-capital balance sheet items minus depreciation. Sort annually.", "rationale": "Earnings composed largely of non-cash accruals are less persistent and more likely to reverse, so the market overvalues high-accrual firms.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (earnings backed by cash)"}, {"name": "Capital Expenditure Intensity Shock", "construction": "Compute current-year capital expenditures (CAPX) scaled by average gross PP&E, minus the prior three-year average of the same ratio. Rank each June.", "rationale": "Firms sharply ramping investment tend to overinvest at cyclical peaks and subsequently deliver lower returns as free cash flow deteriorates.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (restrained investment)"}, {"name": "Gross Profitability Scaled by Assets", "construction": "Compute (Revenue minus Cost of Goods Sold) divided by total assets (AT), using annual Compustat data. Sort firms cross-sectionally.", "rationale": "Gross profit is a cleaner measure of economic productivity than net income and is not yet reflected in valuations, so highly productive firms earn higher returns.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Net Share Issuance", "construction": "Compute the log growth in split-adjusted shares outstanding over the prior 12 months, using CRSP shares outstanding adjusted by the cumulative adjustment factor. Sort firms each month.", "rationale": "Managers issue shares when equity is overpriced and repurchase when underpriced, so net issuance is a signal of managerial market timing predicting lower future returns for issuers.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (net repurchasers)"}, {"name": "Asset Growth", "construction": "Compute year-over-year percentage growth in total assets (Compustat AT). Rank firms cross-sectionally each June.", "rationale": "Rapid balance-sheet expansion through acquisitions, investment, and working capital reflects overinvestment and diminishing marginal returns, leading to underperformance.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (low asset growth)"}, {"name": "Idiosyncratic Volatility from Market Model", "construction": "For each stock, estimate a market-model regression of daily excess returns on the CRSP value-weighted market return over the prior 60 trading days; take the standard deviation of residuals. Sort monthly.", "rationale": "If arbitrage is limited and investors underdiversify, high-idiosyncratic-risk stocks may be overpriced by lottery-seeking investors, earning lower subsequent returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}, {"name": "Dividend Initiation Momentum", "construction": "Flag firms that changed from paying no dividend in the prior 12 months to paying a positive dividend in the most recent quarter (from CRSP distribution codes). Hold a long portfolio of initiators for 12 months.", "rationale": "Dividend initiation is a credible signal of sustainable earnings and disciplined capital allocation that the market underreacts to.", "higher_returns_for": "firms initiating dividends"}, {"name": "Sales-to-Price with Margin Filter", "construction": "Rank firms on annual Revenue divided by market capitalization, but interact this with operating margin (operating income before depreciation / sales). Go long high sales-to-price firms that also have above-median margins.", "rationale": "Cheap-on-sales firms are undervalued, but conditioning on healthy margins screens out value traps with structurally impaired profitability, sharpening the value premium.", "higher_returns_for": "high sales-to-price combined with high margins"}, {"name": "52-Week High Proximity", "construction": "Compute the ratio of current price to the highest price over the trailing 52 weeks using CRSP daily/weekly data. Rank stocks cross-sectionally each month.", "rationale": "The 52-week high serves as an anchor; investors are reluctant to bid prices past it, causing underreaction to good news and continued outperformance for stocks near their highs.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (price near 52-week high)"}]}
